subject: general
question:
Which of the following method(s) can be used to change the direction of force on a current carying conductor?

(i) Changing the magnitude of current

(ii) Changing the strength of magnetic field

(iii) Changing the direction of current
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A current-carrying conductor encounters a **force** that is **perpendicular** to both the **field **and the** direction of the current flow** when it is exposed to an external **magnetic field**.
 
• When a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field, the **direction of the force** acting on it can be determined using **Fleming's Left Hand Rule**.
 
• The method of **changing the direction of the current **can be used to **change the ****direction of the force** on a current carrying conductor.
 
• The direction of force on a **current carrying conductor **can be reversed by reversing the direction of the current.
